title: Selective Relaxation on Total Debt Servicing Ratio Restrictions
what_it_is: Selective Relaxation on Total Debt Servicing Ratio Restrictions

sections.label: Total Debt Servicing Ratio framework
sections.summary: Under the TDSR framework, a borrower's monthly loan instalments should not exceed 60% of monthly income, applying to any property loan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Under the Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR) framework, a borrower's monthly loan instalments should not exceed 60% of his monthly income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The 60% threshold applies to any property loan regardless of whether it is a loan for purchasing a property or a loan secured on an unencumbered property.

sections.label: Exceptional TDSR exceedance approvals
sections.summary: Current rules are the default, but financial institutions may approve property loans exceeding the 60% TDSR in exceptional cases via credit committees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Therefore, it is more prudent to have our current rules as the default position.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: However, financial institutions may approve property loan applications where the borrowers' TDSR exceed Page: 12 60% in exceptional cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Such exceptions must be approved by the financial institutions' credit committees, in line with the policies set by their board of directors.

sections.label: MAS review of TDSR concerns
sections.summary: MAS should review TDSR as some face hardship; TDSR does not apply to company-named loans, and assets and income streams are considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, perhaps, MAS should review this because I think there is some ground concern and some people are having a hard time now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: There are some circumstances, for example, if the borrower runs a company, is a sole proprietor or SME boss and the loan is raised in the name of the company, actually the TDSR does not apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For others, there are also some circumstances, such as they hold other assets, debentures, bonds, coins, gold and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: MAS and the banks do take into account that this can also be income-generating and can also be counted as income stream.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Lastly, there are others, maybe the cases that the Member has encountered, where they need to reduce their fully-paid-for property to re-mortgage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We have received similar feedback and will study them carefully.
